The new New York Knicks forward brought the house down at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday, when he soared for an emphatic putback dunk off a miss from behind the arc by teammate Landry Shamet in the first half of their game against the visiting Chicago Bulls. To make space on the roster for Knecht, the Knicks waived former Kansas Jayhawks star Kevin McCullar Jr . item.title: Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool
item.description: When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind. Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win. But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory. By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten. Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy". After Liverpool let three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt spoke of how he had encouraged Fenerbahce's players to embrace the never-say-die mindset that allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past. He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final, and spent six years at Anfield. "We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win." He and Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it. After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this. On their overnight flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out. "It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened." All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces. Two were scored by Englishmen. Former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood benefited from a slice of luck when his free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet in the first half for Fenerbahce's first equaliser, and Liverpool only had themselves to blame when Cody Gakpo's header took the ball past Alisson and gave Birmingham-born Archie Brown a tap in to make it 2-2. Six minutes later, Liverpool made a mess of Brown's looping ball in the box and Vedat Muriqi beat three players in red and headed past Alisson. "They are cheap goals. item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) shoots against Miami Heat center Bam Adebayo (13) during the second half at Crypto.com Arena. Cameron Carr, the 6-foot-5 wing from Baylor, watched Luka Dončić light up the court and decided the Slovenian is the real deal. Carr told a reporter on Wednesday that he has known since college that Dončić moves in slow motion, yet it just works for him. This young player is not just watching; he is soaking up every bit of wisdom from the best scorer in the NBA. Carr averaged 18.9 points in his only year at Baylor, so he knows what it takes to put the ball in the hoop. He admitted he is in awe of how Dončić plays at his own pace, never getting sped up by defenders. According to the New York Post , Carr said, “I don’t know how it works, but it works. He plays at his own pace; he doesn’t get sped up. It’s impossible to take the ball from him — I don’t know how it works.” That is a bold statement from a guy who has only played two minutes in the league, but he sees something special in Dončić. The Mind Game Changes Everything It is not just the points that impress Carr; it is the way Dončić thinks during the game. The rookie believes that being around such a sharp mind helps everyone on the team improve. Carr noted that watching how Dončić processes the game sharpens his own play and that of those around him. He even joked that he asks Dončić every game if he meant to bank in a three-pointer, and the star always says he did it on purpose. That kind of confidence is hard to fake when you are facing double-teams all night. Dončić is currently averaging a league-high 38.3 points per game, along with 8.1 assists and eight rebounds. His scoring pace is so high that if he keeps it up, he would break Wilt Chamberlain’s all-time record for points per minute set back in 1961. Heat coach Erik Spoelstra admitted after a recent win that Dončić “can make plays, every play in the book that you need to make as a point-of-attack guy. You have to pick him up 30 feet. item.description: The hype train is in full motion with No. 1 Miami slated to face off against No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend on NBC and Peacock this Saturday. Heading into the weekend fresh off the first College Football Playoff rankings release, there's no shortage of storylines for what could be one of the season's most consequential matchups. Ahead of Saturday's highly-anticipated clash, look back at the storied history between both historic programs. How to watch No. 1 Miami vs. No. 11 Notre Dame: TV, live stream, preview for Saturday’s game With major College Football Playoff implications at stake, a storied rivalry will continue with coverage on NBC and Peacock. Nate Ryan , Notre Dame vs. Miami football history, rivalry The Notre Dame Fighting Irish and Miami Hurricanes first clashed helmets over seven decades ago, in 1955. Notre Dame posted a 14-0 victory in what would be the first of 28 meetings between the two schools, and the beginning of a fierce rivalry that heated up in the 1970s and peaked in the late 1980s. While Notre Dame and Miami only faced off only three times during the 1960s, they battled every single year from 1971-1990 (excluding 1986). At first, the Fighting Irish ruled the rivalry with an iron fist, going 12-1-1 against the Hurricanes through 1980. However, this is when the tide began to shift. The Hurricanes would go on to win five of the next six matchups leading up to 1988, when the most famous meeting of the rivalry would occur: the ‘Catholics vs. Convicts’ game. The end of the 1980s also marked a cooling of tensions between the two squads. They only played each other once during the entirety of the 1990s, taking a 20-year hiatus before meeting again in 2010, 2012, 2016, 2017, 2025, and now 2026. item.title: Ball State football falls to UMass in MACtion overtime heartbreaker
item.description: Ball State football got its midweek MACtion slate started with a brutal road loss. Ball State (3-6, 2-3 MAC) suffered a 31-30 overtime defeat on the road at UMass (5-4, 2-3 MAC) , putting their season on the ropes as far as qualifying for a bowl game. The Cardinals ended a two-game winning streak and are now 1-12 on the road under head coach Mike Uremovich. The Minutemen, meanwhile, snapped a four-game losing streak and earned their first home win over an FBS opponent in 20 games. Ball State executed a two-minute drill to tie the game late in regulation and force overtime at 24-24. The Cardinals got the ball first and scored quickly, but kicker Brody Boehm sent the extra point wide left. UMass scored even quicker, and kicker Derek Morris converted on his extra point to give the Minutemen the victory. More: Ball State football coach Mike Uremovich blasts 24-team CFP, US Congress With six losses on the year, Ball State cannot afford another loss over its final three games in order to reach the six wins required for bowl eligibility. The Cardinals have not made a bowl game since 2021 and have not won one since 2020. Here are three takeaways from Ball State football's road loss to UMass on MACtion. Reemergence of penalties hurts Ball State Ball State has been one of the most penalized teams in the MAC this season with 64 total flags on the year entering MACtion, but the Cardinals appeared to have cleaned things up in that department during their recent two-game winning streak with six penalties against Bowling Green and seven against Sacramento State. The yellow flags reappeared on Wednesday night, as the Cardinals were flagged 10 times for 95 yards. The most damning rash of penalties came on UMass' first touchdown drive, in which the Minutemen drove 80 yards for a touchdown and got 45 of those yards via penalties against the Ball State defense. The offense didn't fare much better with the flags, as the Cardinals consistently found themselves behind the sticks facing third-and-long scenarios. Ball State averaged 9.3 yards to go on third downs, on which they went 6-for-14. Defense wins turnover battle but still leaky UMass entered this matchup with the best turnover margin in the MAC at +7, but it was Ball State who won the turnover battle with two key forced fumbles. Linebacker Mikeah Webster was involved in each one, as he recovered a ball that was stripped by defensive back Gabe Aramboles in the second quarter, then punched out a ball that was recovered by defensive end Ben Marsh in the third quarter. The Cardinals were unable to capitalize on the first turnover, but scored a touchdown two plays after the second one. However, the Cardinals' defense still proved susceptible to giving up explosive plays through the air, which UMass quarterback Pop Watson took advantage of on the Minutemen's scoring drives. item.title: Miami Hurricanes star Malachi Toney undergoing surgery
item.description: Oct 17, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) warms up before a game against the Florida State Seminoles at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Hurricanes have been the best team in college football this season, starting 8-0 and debuting at No. 1 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. But the Hurricanes are now heading into their biggest game of the year without their best offensive player. Star wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered an ankle injury at practice on Wednesday, and it has since been revealed that he will need surgery to repair the injury. He’s reportedly set to miss Saturday’s top-15 showdown against Notre Dame, though there’s hope that he could return in time for the College Football Playoff. Toney Injured at Practice Miami’s Wednesday practice was supposed to be just another day of preparation for Notre Dame. Instead, the Hurricanes’ star wideout went down, putting his status for the game in serious doubt . According to On3’s Brett McMurphy, Toney rolled his ankle after getting caught up in a play with a cornerback. Miami confirmed the injury in a statement shortly after. “Malachi Toney sustained an injury during Wednesday’s practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team’s medical staff,” Miami said in a statement, via On3 . “We will share additional updates as appropriate.” Needless to say, losing Toney would be a massive blow for the Hurricanes. The sophomore has 73 catches, the most among Power 4 receivers, for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this season. He’s also been one of the faces of the Heisman Trophy race alongside his quarterback, Darian Mensah. Toney was just as productive as a freshman last season, leading the FBS with 109 catches and setting a Miami single-season record with 1,211 receiving yards as the Hurricanes reached the national championship game. His breakout performance came in the 2025 season opener against Notre Dame, when he caught six passes for 82 yards and a touchdown in a 27-24 win. Toney Getting Surgery Unfortunately for Miami, the news only got worse as the day went on. item.title: State semifinal ending for DeWitt boys soccer fueled by October meeting
item.description: WATERFORD — Joe Ishraidi sensed a shift was needed. The energy within his DeWitt boys soccer program wasn't sitting well with the 12th year coach. So instead of taking the field for practice the day after their Oct. 7 CAAC Silver Cup finals loss to Mason, the Panthers had a team meeting. They aired things out with players and coaches being brutally honest with each other. And once the coaches left, the players talked on their own led by the seniors. "We wrote a bunch of stuff down on a whiteboard and we all signed it," DeWitt senior goalkeeper Vince Rose said. "I know it's a little cliché, but I think it worked. We started to care for each other and fight for our brothers." That meeting provided the spark for what turned out to be the Panthers' deepest playoff run since reaching the state semifinals in 2021. That tournament run came to an end Wednesday, November 4 with a 3-2 loss to No. 6-ranked Warren De La Salle in a Division 2 state semifinal at Waterford Kettering High School. But despite the ending, the last few weeks proved to Rose, Ishraidi and others in the program what is possible when all are on the same page "I think it just shows the power of guys buying in and being willing to work towards something that's bigger than themselves," Ishraidi said. "I couldn't have said that a month ago. We had a great conversation as a team, and they all decided to start focusing in and work hard in practice and that we're going to execute everything we talk about in practice, It's amazing what can happen when you have 25 guys that buy in." The way the Panthers (13-5-5) came together over the last few weeks was on display in Wednesday's semifinal. DeWitt fell into an early two-goal deficit in the opening 10 minutes. But they kept fighting, scoring a goal in the middle stages of the opening half when Mason Raborn found the back of the net. That fight continued in the second half and DeWitt eventually tied the game at 2 with 4:17 remaining on a goal by freshman Jake Wever. Warren De La Salle broke that tie with a goal with 55 seconds remaining off a corner kick that ultimately led to the end of the road for the Panthers. And while the ending stung, Rose is proud of the journey over the last few weeks that included this year's team adding a layer to DeWitt's postseason success. The Panthers knocked off No. 3-ranked Lansing Eastern in a district final on the way to capturing a third regional title since 2020. DeWitt captured a seventh district title in eight season this fall. "We were kind of the Cinderella story almost," Rose said. "We were underdogs back in (the) district. I'm just really proud of the way we showed up for each other." Contact Brian Calloway at bcalloway@lsj.com. Follow him on X @brian_calloway. item.title: Browns’ Shedeur Sanders appears to send Saints defense a warning with cheeky response
item.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Shedeur Sanders appears to have sent a message to the New Orleans Saints defence after delivering a cheeky response when asked about the unit ahead of the Cleveland Browns’ next game. The 24-year-old could be in line for his first start of the 2026 campaign after Deshaun Watson entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. Cleveland are coming off a disappointing 27-6 defeat to the Pittsburgh Steelers, making the quarterback situation an important talking point ahead of their meeting with New Orleans. Shedeur Sanders hints at confidence against New Orleans Saints defence Sanders was asked about the Saints’ defence during his media availability and chose not to give a straightforward assessment. Instead, the Browns quarterback offered a cryptic response that suggested he was feeling confident about the matchup. “Yeah, I’ve seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something,” Sanders said. He then added: “I’m maturing, you know what I’m saying? I’m maturing. Like, I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I’m just going to smile.” The comments have attracted attention, with Sanders seemingly hinting that he has spotted something he believes Cleveland can exploit. Sanders has spent much of the season watching from the sidelines after losing the starting job to Watson. He has appeared in just two games, completing all three of his pass attempts for two yards. However, he did get an opportunity to start during the second half of Cleveland’s 2025 campaign after initially beginning his rookie season as a backup. His numbers were mixed, completing 120 of 212 passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Now, with Watson’s availability uncertain, Sanders could have another opportunity to show what he can do as the Browns’ starting quarterback. The Saints’ defence has struggled this season, but Sanders’ comments could give New Orleans extra motivation heading into the contest. Whether he gets the nod remains dependent on Watson’s recovery and clearance from concussion protocol. If Sanders does start, he will have a chance to back up his confident words on the field. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Maddie Meyer BOSTON (AP) — Paul George scored 25 points and had five 3-pointers, Derrick White added 24 points and seven assists, and the Boston Celtics beat the Milwaukee Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday night. Tyler Herro scored 18 of his 25 points during the third quarter for the Bucks, who fell to 1-7, including 0-4 on the road. Jaime Jaquez Jr. added 18 points. Baylor Scheierman had nine points and 11 rebounds off the bench for the Celtics, who survived a scare after being pushed by one of the NBA’s weaker teams. Boston never trailed through three quarters, opening a 22-point advantage in the second quarter, leading by 21 at halftime and eight entering the fourth. Milwaukee’s best stretch came during the third quarter, with a 26-12 run to make it a single-digit game. When Ryan Rollins slammed home two of his 13 points, the Bucks trailed 91-89 with 8:17 remaining. George threw the ball away coming out of a timeout, with Milwaukee’s Nate Ament racing the other way for a layup that tied it at 91. item.title: Xavier edges Wilbur Cross to capture eighth SCC boys soccer championship
item.description: Xavier head coach Brian Fitzgerald and team celebrate after defeating Wilbur Cross 2-1 in the SCC Boys Soccer Final at West Haven High School in West Haven, Conn., Wednesday, November 4, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HAVEN - When Rays Kisaku came to Xavier, he said he promised something to his boys soccer coach. "I told my coach (Brian Fitzgerald) I would win it (a championship) for him," Kisaku said. It took three seasons, but Kisaku cashed in on that promise. He scored in the early stages of the second half, the game-winning goal, for top seed Xavier in a 2-1 victory over No. 3 Wilbur Cross Wednesday at Ken Strong Stadium. The Falcons (17-0-2), the No. 2 team in the GametimeCT rankings , won their eighth SCC championship, fifth in this decade alone. After winning four straight from 2020-23, Xavier missed out the last two seasons. "It's a goal every season to win the division, win the conference and win states," Fitzgerald said. "We tell the guys from the get-go, they know the expectations are high. They work, they work for it. We hold them to a high standard and every year that culture doesn't change, that standard doesn't change." This was the first appearance in an SCC championship game for Wilbur Cross (14-3-2). The Governors salvaged a 1-1 tie with Xavier during the regular season. "It's bittersweet because we came here to win. The kids battled their rear ends off," Wilbur Cross coach Scott Raffone said. "I'm so proud of them, so proud of the effort." Kisaku scored just 1 minute, 26 seconds into the second half. John Staron, who scored Xavier's tying goal, had the initial shot. Wilbur Cross goalkeeper Luis Rodriguez kept the Governors in it with eight saves. One of those came on Staron's shot. But Rodriguez could not control it. "Whenever he shoots, I kind of just run for it. I always know it's going to be on frame, so on that play I saw it, the keeper is bound to deflect it," Kisaku said. "From then, I just chased it down and put it in the back of the net." Kisaku believed the defense would hold up and the Falcons proved him right. Xavier goalkeeper Roldofo Fraschilla was named the SCC tournament Most Outstanding Player. He allowed just the one first-half goal to Wilbur Cross in the three-game tournament. "They pressured us in a way where I was on my toes until the very last second," Fraschilla said. "At no point did I let my guard down. "I was always on high alert. I don't play this sport for awards, I play it for my team. I'm so proud of these guys. This group of very accomplished players, I can't wait to see where all their careers take them." Leo Castellano scored the opening goal for Wilbur Cross off a direct kick. Player of the Game Rays Kisaku, Xavier: Junior buried the rebound off an initial shot to put Xavier ahead to stay, 2-1 in the second half. item.title: Sixers roll on to down Pistons, Knicks gore Bulls
item.description: Jaylen Brown's 30-point performance helped Philadelphia down the Detroit Pistons in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference duel on Wednesday (Gregory Shamus) Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid combined for 56 points as the Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Detroit Pistons 112-106 in their heavyweight top-of-the-table NBA Eastern Conference clash on Wednesday. Brown finished with 30 points and Embiid added 26 to give the Sixers another impressive road win that moved them to 8-1 at the top of the standings, with Detroit (6-2) in second. Brown and Embiid led another balanced offensive performance from Philadelphia, who saw all five starters reach double figures. LeBron James added a double-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists while Tyrese Maxey drained three three-pointers on his way to a 19-point haul. Brown, who arrived from the Boston Celtics in the offseason, said he was "still adjusting" to his new team-mates. "I'm still figuring it out," Brown said, before paying tribute to the performance of 41-year-old team-mate James. "LeBron has been great," Brown said. "To see what he's doing at his age makes sense for LeBron James, but for nobody else would it make sense." The Sixers moved into the lead towards the end of the first quarter and kept their noses in front for the remainder of the game, stretching the lead to 18 points before a late rally from Detroit. Duncan Robinson led the Pistons with 27 points while Cade Cunningham added 26. The reigning champion New York Knicks scored their biggest win of the season with a 135-105 blowout over the Chicago Bulls at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks, who have made a slow start to the new campaign, improved to 4-4 after a dazzling 33-point performance from Jalen Brunson, who drained five three-pointers while making 10-of-17 from the field. O.G. Anunoby scored 18 points while Karl-Anthony Towns added 17 for a Knicks team who led by as many as 44 points midway through the third quarter. In Boston, the Milwaukee Bucks threatened to pull off a huge comeback before finally succumbing 109-102 to the Celtics. Paul George (25 points) and Derrick White (24) led the scoring for Boston, who appeared to be cruising after leading by 20 early in the third quarter. But a 38-point third quarter from Milwaukee flipped the script and the Bucks edged into a 96-95 lead with five minutes remaining. item.title: Eagles pull the plug on Tanner McKee, turn to new QB
item.description: PHILADELPHIA — The Eagles are benching quarterback Tanner McKee for Joe Milton III, according to an ESPN report. After Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve, McKee became the starter in Week 6. He completed 72 of his 114 passes for 638 yards and two touchdowns. He also threw two interceptions. McKee finished with a 30.6 QBR and a 76.7 passer rating. The Eagles have lost the last three games with McKee as the starter, but it’s surprising that they are changing quarterbacks before the bye week. McKee wasn’t good, but it’s unlikely that Milton will be an upgrade. “Tanner’s our guy,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said on Monday. “We’re not making any changes there. Again, how do we find solutions? That could be within scheme, that could be within how our schedule is, practice plays. Everything’s on the table for us in that aspect. But right now, this is where we are and we’re trying to find solutions there. We’re looking at everything as far as what we can do differently as coaches.” The Eagles signed Milton off the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16 to serve as the backup. item.title: Bryson DeChambeau Has Big Problem Amid LIV 2.0 Failure
item.description: WESTFIELD, INDIANA - AUGUST 23: Bryson DeChambeau of Crushers GC plays his shot from the second tee during day four of LIV Golf Indianapolis at The Club at Chatham Hills on August 23, 2026 in Westfield, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty Bryson DeChambeau might have more to sort out than where he wants to play golf next season. The two-time U.S. Open champion continued backing LIV Golf’s next chapter while several familiar faces looked elsewhere. Now, the collapse of that plan could leave him with a particularly uncomfortable conversation about his own future. DeChambeau remains one of golf’s biggest attractions. However, his popularity doesn’t answer the question of how he gets back to a regular schedule against the world’s best players. His recent support for LIV 2.0 adds another complication. Wednesday’s reporting revealed that prospective financial backer BC Partners had abandoned its rescue plan after failing to secure enough player commitments. That leaves LIV facing liquidation and its remaining golfers searching for answers about 2027 and beyond. On Golf Channel Wednesday evening, Todd Lewis asked analyst Rex Hoggard what comes next for DeChambeau. Hoggard pointed to a difference between his situation and Jon Rahm’s. “I think [DeChambeau] is going to be the most compelling story moving forward,” Hoggard said. Rahm has already expressed a willingness to accept consequences as he works toward playing elsewhere. DeChambeau, meanwhile, had continued supporting the league that was supposed to give him a home. Rahm Has Already Started Looking Beyond LIV Golf Hoggard explained that Rahm hadn’t immediately embraced the conditions surrounding his next move. Nevertheless, the Spaniard eventually made his intentions clear. “[Rahm] pushed back on the idea that there was gonna be some stipulations, and some restrictions and some fines going back to the DP World Tour, but eventually, he got around to, ‘Okay, I’m going to pay these fines. I want to play the DP World Tour in 2027.’ Keep in mind, the Ryder Cup is part of that conversation as well,” Hoggard mentioned. That doesn’t guarantee Rahm a PGA Tour return. It does, however, give him a stated direction for next season. He has acknowledged that returning to another circuit could require concessions. DeChambeau’s circumstances look different because he was backing a future that now appears unlikely to happen. While others moved away from LIV, he remained a potential centerpiece of its proposed relaunch. “For Bryson, I think this is an entirely different animal because he has made it clear, you’re right, it seems as if based on his comments this week, he was committed, to whenever [LIV] 2.0 was going to go,” Hoggard stated. “He was going to the one that was leading the charge. He was going to be that [star] attraction that could have made 2.0 work.” The timing matters. item.title: Josh Jacobs Addresses Possibility of Future Further Suspension
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers warms up prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty The off-the-field situation for Green Bay Packers‘ Josh Jacobs went from bad to worse on Sat Oct. 31 when it was reported that three other women have accused the All-Pro running back of domestic abuse, two of which were alleged to have occurred in 2021 and 2022, when Jacobs was still on the Las Vegas Raiders. Jacobs spoke out about the new abuse allegations on Nov. 4, before commenting on how he feels about a potential further looming suspension in the works. Josh Jacobs after the latest allegations of physical abuse against him: “With all the evidence that we have and that they have, at this point it’s not one of those things where I’m sitting back on my hands like, ‘OK, am I gonna play this week?’” “It’s really just up to them to… pic.twitter.com/v7V0P75wa9 — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) November 4, 2026 Josh Jacobs Comments on Potential For Missing More Time “With all the evidence that we have and that they have, at this point it’s not one of those things where I’m sitting back on my hands like, ‘OK, am I gonna play this week?’, it’s like I already know what it is.” Jacobs said on Wednesday, per The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman. “It’s really just up to them to make their final decision, but I’m not worried about feeling like I’m a miss any more time than I already have.” Although Jacobs accepts that he might well end up being suspended for more time, following the accusations of three more women, it appears that his attitude is to focus solely on what he can control. How Much Longer Might the NFL Suspend Josh Jacobs For? In terms of further suspension, there is not much historical evidence that would give a big clue as to what the NFL might do, although much of that might change depending on if Jacobs is charged with any crimes or misdemeanors following the further accusations reported last weekend. Deshaun Watson was accused of sexual misconduct by 25 women prior to his suspension, along with another two more afterwards, and he was barred for a total of 11 games in 2022. Atlanta Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr., on the other hand, was recently handed an eight-game suspension after being charged with three felonies and a misdemeanor after a domestic incident with WNBA star Rickea Jackson back in February. So it is not clear exactly how the NFL might proceed with further discipline, if they do at all. The future is anything but certain for Jacobs at this moment.
